filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain a federal EIN from the IRS online.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) on the CA SOS bizfile portal, then apply for the EIN. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 LLC, $25 corporation).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and register the fictitious business name (DBA) with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register within 30 days of starting business; fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55–$700 plus $4 state fee). The BAN is required by every other city department. File the FBN statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail (photo ID required), then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC need the filed FBN statement.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: File the DPH plan check for the kitchen (if remodeling) and apply for the health permit to operate, with proof of a certified food safety manager.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit kitchen plans, equipment specs, finishes and the menu to DPH online. The 2026–27 plan check fee is $828 (small remodel, 3 hrs) to $2,207 (new restaurant, 8 hrs). One owner or employee must pass an accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, $100–$250) within 60 days of opening. After plan approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance. The health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license for bars/restaurants in 2026–28) is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and the certified manager is on staff. Do not serve food to the public before the permit is issued.

timeline_cost.notes: The day range is the time to obtain the discretionary approvals when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the catalog and the one comparable with a filing date, which took 538 days but is an outlier) and Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days per the catalog). The building permit (14–120 days per the catalog) and health permit (14–45 days) follow approval of the CUA and are not discretionary hearings, so their time is not the long pole. Cost range covers the CUA application fee (~$3,150 CPI-adjusted), the POE application fee ($2,708 in 2026–27), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation for soundproofing and tenant improvements), and the health plan check and permit ($828–$2,207 plan check, $470 permit application). The total does not include the acoustic consultant's fee (likely $2,000–$5,000 for a report and soundproofing plan), the architect's fee for building permit plans (typically $5,000–$15,000 for a bar/entertainment remodel), or construction costs (soundproofing, finishes, equipment). These are professional service and construction costs, not government permit fees, so they are not in the range above. The CUA is the critical path: 4–10 months including pre-application meeting, filing, environmental review, neighborhood notice, hearing scheduling and the 30-day appeal period. File it immediately after the entity is formed and the BAN is obtained. The POE application should be filed after the CUA is approved so that the Planning referral can reference the CUA approval.

records_summary: 1237 Polk St is an established bar (McTeague's Saloon) in the Polk Street NCD, holding an active Type 48 license since 2008 under a Conditional Use Authorization granted in 2008 (Motion #17569). The space was previously a restaurant/bar with a Type 47 license dating to 1986. The zoning pathway confirms that a bar is a conditional use on the first story in NCD-POLK, and because an active Type 48 exists at this address the space is read as a bar; the proposal to add entertainment to the existing bar is not a change of use. The block is extremely dense: 31 food/drink businesses and 21 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 16 bars in that radius. Four dated use decisions for bars, restaurants, and entertainment within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years show 1 approval and 3 approvals with conditions; no denials, but too few cases (N=4) for a meaningful approval rate.
